clue.text: What's represented by mus or xis not a current issue

definitions.text: What's represented by mus or xis
definitions.meaning: the Greek letters mus and xis, read backwards, spell SUM and SIX, which are numbers backwards
an old edition of a magazine or paper, no longer on sale as the latest

explanation.surface: A puzzle about Greek letters drifting into a remark on old magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: Mus and xis written in reverse give SUM and SIX, so each is a number back to front; the phrase also means an out-of-date edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a past edition of a periodical, no longer the latest one offered for sale.

clue.text: Bishop withdrawing praise

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
withdrawing, in the sense of taking away or subtracting, gives less (as in 'ten less two')

explanation.surface: A churchman takes back the compliments he once gave.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to glorify or extol God, as in hymns that call on all to give thanks.

clue.text: Led like Batman catching train — Robin's first to go

indicators.note: catching means the caped word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: Batman is the Caped Crusader, so like him is caped

indicators.note: to go tells us that letter is taken out of the word train
first picks the opening letter of the word Robin's

explanation.surface: Batman leads the way while snagging a train, with Robin dropped from the outing.
explanation.walkthrough: Batman's cape is the clue; 'Robin' here is just a source for its first letter, not a partner to add.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who led a team or a ship was its skipper or commander.

clue.text: Identity removed for Queen in secret after latest PR event

indicators.note: after places the news word in front of what follows, as the piece that comes first

parts.note: the latest is the news, as in 'have you heard the latest?'

indicators.note: removed for means one piece is taken out and another put in its place

parts.note: a confidence is a secret told in trust
ID is short for identity
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A spin doctor swaps a name for royalty in confidential papers before a press launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secret' is a noun here: a confidence. 'in' just links the swap to the word it works on.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a briefing where journalists are invited to hear and question, a staple of public relations.

clue.text: Bellicose poet of ancient times

definitions.meaning: the Roman epigrammatist of the first century AD

explanation.surface: A combative versifier from antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym for warlike, and also the name of a Latin writer of witty epigrams.

clue.text: Strange bore in river rising — it does so at surprising times

definitions.text: it does so at surprising times

indicators.note: in means the rearranged letters sit inside the turned river name
rising, in a down clue, means the river's name is read from the bottom up

parts.note: the Wye is a river on the England-Wales border

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of bore are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An odd tidal bore surges up a river, as bores do at unexpected moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' turns BORE into EBRO (itself a Spanish river), which goes 'in' EYW, the Wye written upwards by 'rising'. 'it does so' means it rises.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the hairy arch above the eye goes up when someone is taken aback.

clue.text: Speaker's full agreement

indicators.note: Speaker's signals that a word as heard is the one wanted

parts.note: full means packed, as a packed hall

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker gives complete assent.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a treaty or deal struck between parties.

clue.text: Simple refusal stops a bit of bother

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the refusal goes inside

parts.note: a bit of means any, as in 'is there any milk?'
the plainest way to refuse is no

explanation.surface: A curt no puts an end to minor trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to irritate or pester someone, as a nagging worry does.

clue.text: Team in trade adapted my way of stuffing goose etc

indicators.note: in means the team goes inside the rearranged letters
adapted means the letters of trade are reworked into a new order

parts.note: a team of eleven is an XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A team reworking the business of a cook preparing the Christmas bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the craft of preserving and mounting dead animals, so geese and the like are literally stuffed.

clue.text: To support ace intellectual I'm adopting singular orthodoxy

parts.note: to fund is to support financially
A is the card abbreviation for ace
mental means of the intellect

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the letters of I'm hold the next piece

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Backing a brilliant thinker who embraces a rigid creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: strict adherence to the basic tenets of a faith, opposed to liberal reinterpretation.

clue.text: Allow no time at all for worker to rise

indicators.note: no, with at all, says every instance of the time letter is dropped
at all extends the removal to each occurrence, not just one

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
to tower is to rise high
T is the physics abbreviation for time; both of them go

explanation.surface: A boss permits no break whatever so the staff can get on.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMP plus TOWER gives TEMPTOWER; 'no time at all' strips both Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to authorise or give someone the power to do something.

clue.text: One animal clipped before another on farm — it occurs twice a year

indicators.note: clipped means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an equine is a horse, one kind of animal
an ox is another animal found on a farm

explanation.surface: A horse with a trimmed coat stands before an ox on a farm, and the event recurs every six months.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the day when night and day are of equal length, in spring and in autumn.

clue.text: Man shooting on street bags one more stiff

indicators.note: on means the archer sits on, so follows, the street abbreviation in this across entry

parts.note: ST is the address abbreviation for street

indicators.note: bags means holds, so the archer contains the next piece

parts.note: an archer is a man shooting arrows
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A gunman in the street grabs another, even more rigid than before.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative: laundry with more starch is more rigid, and a formal manner can be called that too.

clue.text: Lacking in interest nowadays, and spirit

parts.note: a dry lecture is one lacking interest
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Modern life is dull, and so is the mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a tree nymph of Greek myth, one sort of nature spirit.

clue.text: Country home beyond mountain

indicators.note: beyond means the home word comes after the mountain

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
in means at home

explanation.surface: A homeland lies past a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a West African nation lying between Togo and Nigeria.

clue.text: Itinerant trader's youngster in Cumbria?

definitions.meaning: a street seller pushing his goods about on a handcart
a lad from Barrow-in-Furness, a town in Cumbria in north-west England

explanation.surface: A travelling hawker is a lad from the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a costermonger selling fruit from a cart, and literally a boy from a Cumbrian town.

clue.text: Secondary fencing involved man coming round with cutting equipment

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the secondary word surrounds the rest

parts.note: lower means secondary, as in a lower rank

indicators.note: coming round means the rearranged letters wrap around the next piece
involved means twisted up, so the letters of man are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tangled wire fence of a lower grade, and a fellow arriving with machinery for the hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges man as ANM, 'coming round' wraps it about W to give AWNM, and 'fencing' sets that inside the secondary word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a garden machine with blades for trimming grass.

clue.text: On the way down, holding up angry looking vagrant

indicators.note: holding means the declining word contains the next piece

parts.note: waning means declining, as the moon does

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the angry word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a face flushed red looks angry

explanation.surface: Someone sinking, red-faced and furious, looks like a tramp.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: roaming without a fixed home, like a drifter.

clue.text: Embarrassed, left abandoning colonist's best friend?

parts.note: red means embarrassed, blushing

indicators.note: abandoning means the left letter is dropped from the colonist

parts.note: a settler is a colonist; the 's reads as 'is' linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A shamed pioneer, deserted by his companion, finds his truest ally.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'best friend' means a dog, as in 'man's best friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dog is man's best friend, and this is a glossy chestnut gundog breed.

clue.text: Stain bottom of post with gloss, not top

indicators.note: bottom of, in a down clue, picks the final letter of post
not top means the first letter is removed

parts.note: varnish is a glossy coating

explanation.surface: Instructions for treating a fence post: gloss the bottom but leave the top bare.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to discolour or sully, as silver dulls or a reputation suffers.

clue.text: To provide fresh cover for agent isn't common

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
ain't is a common, nonstandard form of isn't

explanation.surface: A spy's new cover story is hardly ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: giving a wall or door a new coat is renewing its covering.

clue.text: Last five of nine-month term in French city?

indicators.note: last five of means only the final five letters are kept, the rest being dropped

parts.note: a pregnancy lasts about nine months

explanation.surface: The final stretch of a long gestation, spent in a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a city in Lorraine, north-east France, famous for its Art Nouveau.

clue.text: Veteran squaddie not taking sides

indicators.note: not taking sides means both outer letters are removed

parts.note: a squaddie is a private soldier in the British Army

explanation.surface: An old private stays neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an old-timer, someone of advanced years or long service.

clue.text: After reflection ruler imprisons old slaver

indicators.note: imprisons means holds inside
after reflection means the ruler's word is seen as in a mirror, backwards

parts.note: a lord is a ruler

explanation.surface: A thoughtful monarch jails an elderly slave trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slaver' looks like a slave trader but is the verb meaning to dribble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to let saliva run from the mouth, to dribble.

clue.text: Electrical devices consumer introduced to theatres

indicators.note: introduced to means placed inside

parts.note: reps are repertory theatres
an eater is one who consumes

explanation.surface: Gadgets reach theatres via a shopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: devices that receive a signal and retransmit it amplified, in telegraphy and radio.

clue.text: Shrub from south porter originally removed from college grounds

indicators.note: from south, in a down clue, means reading upwards
removed from means that letter is taken out of the grounds word

parts.note: a campus is the grounds of a college

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of porter

explanation.surface: A bush taken from the southern edge of campus after the porter digs it up.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking P out of CAMPUS leaves CAMUS, which reads upwards as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a shrub or small tree whose red berries give a tart spice.

clue.text: Choir travelling round North on British Airways

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
travelling means moving about, so the letters of choir are rearranged

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A choir flying north on Britain's national airline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British Airways' looks like one name, but B is British and 'Airways' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the two main tubes branching from the windpipe into the lungs.

clue.text: Metal I'd identified primarily pinched by one suspect

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: pinched by means held inside

parts.note: rum means odd or suspect
I'd is taken as written

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of identified

explanation.surface: A detective says the metal he identified was nicked by a dodgy character.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a dense, hard metallic element of the platinum group.

clue.text: Walk back without beginning to cry

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read in the other direction
without beginning means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: an alley is a narrow walk or path

explanation.surface: Walking home without a start, ready to weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to shout or scream loudly.

clue.text: One enterprise going west with wicked witch around?

definitions.text: One enterprise going west with wicked witch around?

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the reversed piece
wicked suggests something twisted, so the letters of witch are rearranged
going west, in an across clue, means read from right to left

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a game is a line of business, as in 'what's your game?'

explanation.surface: A wicked witch hovering over a venture heading west, as in Oz, is the opposite of her art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' turns IGAME into EMAGI; 'wicked' makes WHITC of WITCH, split round it. The whole clue hints at a good witch's spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: beneficent spells, the good kind of sorcery contrasted with the dark arts.
